title: A rock, paper, scissors round
description:
Play rounds against the computer with a `switch`.

```
Your move (rock/paper/scissors): paper
Computer: rock
You win!
Score: you 1, computer 0
```
hints: `String beats = switch (move) { case "rock" -> "scissors"; case "paper" -> "rock"; case "scissors" -> "paper"; default -> null; };` (lesson 1.05).

The starter's `moves` is an array of the three moves (arrays come in lesson 2.02): `moves[0]` is `"rock"`, `moves[1]` `"paper"` and `moves[2]` `"scissors"`. `random.nextInt(3)` gives 0, 1 or 2, so `String computerMove = moves[random.nextInt(3)];` picks one.
requirements: Read moves until the user types `quit`; ignore case.
The computer picks with `new Random(42)` (a fixed seed makes it repeatable).
Decide the winner with a `switch` expression; an unknown move prints `Unknown move` and does not count.
stretch: Play best of five and print the overall winner.
